# CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

## What this is

The Paigasus AI SDK (codename **Helikon**, after Mt Helicon where Pegasus's hoof struck the Hippocrene spring). A Rust SDK for building AI agents. All crates live under the `paigasus-helikon-*` namespace.

The full architectural reference lives in Notion: ["Crate Reference"](https://www.notion.so/355830e8fbaa813c92e8c1aa9985fd3f). Linear project: `Paigasus Helikon` (issues prefixed `SMA-`).

## Common commands

```bash
cargo build --workspace                              # all 14 crates
cargo build --workspace --all-features               # facade with every optional crate
cargo run -p paigasus-helikon-cli --bin helikon
cargo run -p paigasus-helikon-cli --bin paigasus-helikon
```

To reproduce **every** CI gate locally (matches `.github/workflows/ci.yml` job-for-job):

```bash
cargo fmt --all -- --check
cargo clippy --workspace --all-features --all-targets -- -D warnings
cargo test --workspace --all-features
RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo doc --workspace --all-features --no-deps
DOC_COVERAGE_THRESHOLD=80 NIGHTLY_CHANNEL=nightly-2026-05-01 \
  bash scripts/check-doc-coverage.sh                 # requires: rustup toolchain install nightly-2026-05-01
npm ci                                               # once, or after package-lock.json changes
npx markdownlint-cli2                                # reads .markdownlint-cli2.jsonc
bash scripts/check-markdownlint-config.sh            # asserts that config is in force
bash scripts/check-cargo-profile-env-sync.sh         # cargo-visible workflow env is uniform
bash scripts/check-cargo-profile-env-sync-selftest.sh # …and its parser still parses (fmt runs both)
bash scripts/check-release-gaps-selftest.sh            # release gap report + release-plz.yml guards (fmt runs it)
```

The full list lives in `CONTRIBUTING.md` (single source of truth for contributor policies).

## Workspace layout

15 crates under `crates/`. The facade `paigasus-helikon` re-exports `paigasus-helikon-core` unconditionally and the other 12 sibling crates behind Cargo features.

Every crate carries a real implementation and publishes to crates.io; zero name-claim stubs remain (first published in SMA-385, last ascends in SMA-333). Two standing exceptions: `paigasus-helikon-cli` publishes as a **binary** crate — its lib target is internal (`missing_docs` opted out), carries no stability guarantee, and exists only so `cargo install paigasus-helikon-cli` resolves; and `paigasus-helikon-sessions-testkit` is the sole non-published crate, an internal `Session` conformance harness intentionally kept at `0.0.0` with `publish = false`, not a stub awaiting an ascend. Exact versions move every release — read each crate's `Cargo.toml`, don't trust numbers written here.

Workspace inheritance is **mandatory**: per-crate `Cargo.toml`s only set `name`, `description`, and any crate-specific bits. Everything else (`edition`, `rust-version`, `authors`, `license`, `repository`, `homepage`, `keywords`, `categories`) inherits from `[workspace.package]` in the root `Cargo.toml`. Don't hardcode these per-crate.

**Per-crate version is the one exception.** No stubs remain, so the 4-step ascend recipe is now historical — but two caveats still bite any PR that hand-bumps a version:

- **If a crate uses `paigasus-helikon-core` API added in the *same* PR, bump `core` too**, along with its `[workspace.dependencies]` pin and CHANGELOG. `cargo publish --verify` builds the tarball against the **registry** core, so otherwise the publish fails and release-plz deadlocks.
- **Any PR that hand-bumps a sibling must ALSO bump the facade** (`crates/paigasus-helikon/Cargo.toml` version + its self-pin + CHANGELOG). release-plz's `dependencies_update` cascade only runs when release-plz itself performs the sibling bump, so a manual bump silently leaves the facade advertising stale dep reqs.
- Feature branches must match the `branch-names` ruleset (`feature/**` or `hotfix/**`); a `chore/**` branch is rejected at push with `GH013 … creations being restricted`.

Full lifecycle, the 4-step recipe, and the SMA-321/SMA-346 postmortems: `docs/runbooks/release-ascend.md`.

Third-party version pins live in `[workspace.dependencies]` (root). Members reference them via `dep.workspace = true`. Internal crate paths are also in `[workspace.dependencies]` so the facade can use `workspace = true` consistently.

## Non-obvious patterns to preserve

- **Feature naming**: kebab-case in `[features]` (`runtime-tokio`), snake-case in `pub use` aliases (`runtime_tokio`). They must stay paired across the facade's `Cargo.toml` and `src/lib.rs`.
- **`paigasus-helikon-cli` uses `autobins = false`** because the `paigasus-helikon` (hyphen) binary maps to `src/bin/paigasus_helikon.rs` (underscore — hyphens are illegal in Rust filenames). Removing `autobins = false` reintroduces a phantom `paigasus_helikon` binary that conflicts with the explicit `[[bin]]` entry.
- **`paigasus-helikon-macros` is a proc-macro crate from day one** (`[lib] proc-macro = true`). Don't convert it to a regular lib even though it currently has no macros.
- **The `paigasus-helikon` facade lib shares its name with the `paigasus-helikon` CLI binary by design** (Notion ref's "fully-qualified shim alias"). This produces a non-fatal `cargo doc` filename-collision warning. Don't "fix" it by renaming either — both names are user-facing API. The accepted future fix is `doc = false` on the CLI binary entry.
- **License is dual `Apache-2.0 OR MIT`** (decided 2026-05-20, reversing the 2026-05-16 MIT-only call). Both `LICENSE-APACHE` and `LICENSE-MIT` live at the repo root; the workspace metadata is `license = "Apache-2.0 OR MIT"`. Per Rust ecosystem convention — no Apache-only or MIT-only crates in the workspace. Contributions are accepted under the same dual license by default (the standard inbound-equals-outbound clause is restated in `README.md`).
- **MSRV is `1.94`** (workspace-package level; raised from 1.85 in SMA-329 because sqlx 0.9.0 declares `rust-version = "1.94.0"` — the pre-existing highest floor in the workspace). If a dep raises MSRV, bump `rust-version` to what cargo demands rather than downgrading the dep.
- **Workspace-wide `missing_docs` enforcement** lives in root `Cargo.toml` (`[workspace.lints.rust] missing_docs = "warn"`). Each non-CLI crate opts in with `[lints] workspace = true`. The CLI overrides locally with `[lints.rust] missing_docs = "allow"` and does **not** include `workspace = true` — cargo treats `[lints] workspace = true` and an inline `[lints.<tool>]` table as mutually exclusive. When adding a new crate, copy the opt-in block. When adding a new `pub use` re-export to the facade, give it a `///` doc comment or `-D warnings` will fail the docs job.
- **`cargo msrv` has no `--workspace` flag.** The msrv workflow verifies one representative inheriting crate: `cargo msrv --path crates/paigasus-helikon-core verify`. Because every member uses `rust-version.workspace = true`, success on one is success on all. Don't "fix" the workflow by adding `--workspace`; that's what the first SMA-305 CI run died on.
- **Nightly is date-pinned** (`NIGHTLY_TOOLCHAIN: nightly-2026-05-01` at the workflow `env:` level in `ci.yml`, threaded into the doc-coverage script as `NIGHTLY_CHANNEL`). The rustdoc JSON coverage format is `-Z unstable-options` and can shift between nightlies; floating `nightly` would be a CI footgun. Bumping is a one-line follow-up chore, not an emergency.
- **Bootstrap commits on release infrastructure must use `chore(...)` or `docs(...)` types**, never `feat`/`fix`. release-plz parses every commit since the last per-crate tag — a `feat(workspace): ...` commit that touches every `Cargo.toml` would attribute a bump to every crate. The SMA-307 bootstrap PR followed this rule; the same rule applies to any future `release-plz.toml` or `release-plz.yml` edits.

## Model routing

The general tiering rules are in the global `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md`. Only the repo-specific rules are here.

- **Use Opus for release work.** This covers release-plz, the stub-ascend recipe, a hand-bumped crate version, and any red required gate. A wrong answer breaks a publish; see `docs/runbooks/release-ascend.md`.
- **Haiku can read CI output.** Change to Opus when the question becomes *why* a required gate is red.

## Workflow conventions

- Branch per Linear issue: `feature/<sma-####>-<kebab-title>`. The branch name is pre-computed in each Linear ticket's `gitBranchName` field.
- Design artifacts per ticket (`docs/superpowers/specs/YYYY-MM-DD-<topic>-design.md`, `docs/superpowers/plans/YYYY-MM-DD-<topic>.md`) land on the feature branch alongside the implementation — not pre-merged to `main`.
- **Keep the public mdBook (`docs/book/`) current — update it in the same PR as any user-facing change.** Before opening a PR, check whether the work changes public API, the quickstart/example flow, the crate roster (incl. a stub crate ascending to published), or a documented concept; if so, bring the affected `docs/book/src/*.md` page(s) into line on the same branch. The book is published from `main` and drifts silently otherwise — it sat as the untouched SMA-311 scaffold (13/17 pages still `> **Stub.**`) through all of Stage 1 before anyone noticed; SMA-423 is the one-time catch-up, and this rule keeps the backlog from rebuilding. A pure-internal change (refactor, CI, deps, release plumbing) needs no book edit — but make that a conscious call, not a silent skip. `mdbook build docs/book` must stay clean (`[output.linkcheck] warning-policy = "error"`).
- **Keep crate `README.md` files current — update the affected crate's README in the same PR as any change to its public surface.** Each of the ten published crates' `README.md` is its crates.io (and docs.rs landing-sidebar) page — no crate sets an explicit `readme`, so Cargo uses the default `README.md`. Before opening a PR, for every crate the work touches check whether the change affects that crate's public API / usage example, its install or feature story, or its published status (a stub ascending to published, a renamed/added feature flag); if so, bring its `crates/<crate>/README.md` into line on the same branch — and also the facade `crates/paigasus-helikon/README.md` and the root `README.md` whenever the crate roster or the feature → module map changes. README install snippets deliberately use drift-free `cargo add` (no hardcoded versions), so a routine version bump alone needs no README edit. Like the mdBook, the READMEs drift silently otherwise — they sat as untouched 3-line SMA-304 stubs (`Stub — see SMA-304`) through all of Stage 1 while ten crates shipped real implementations; SMA-424 is the one-time catch-up, and this rule keeps the backlog from rebuilding. A pure-internal change (refactor, CI, deps, release plumbing) needs no README edit — but make that a conscious call, not a silent skip.
- Commit prefix: `<type>(<scope>): SMA-### <message>` (e.g. `feat(facade): SMA-304 ...`).
- **PR titles must satisfy two independent rules from `pr-title.yml`** (`amannn/action-semantic-pull-request`):
  1. **Full Conventional Commits format.** The action enforces a valid `type(scope):` prefix from the action's configured `types` list — independent of the subject regex. `SMA-317 add anthropic provider` (no prefix) fails; `feat(providers-anthropic): SMA-317 add anthropic provider` passes.
  2. **Subject must start lowercase after the `SMA-###` prefix.** The `subjectPattern: ^([A-Z]{2,4}-\d+ )?[^A-Z].+$` rejects `feat(core): SMA-314 LlmAgent + ...` because `L` is uppercase; lead the subject with a lowercase verb (`add`, `wire`, `pin`, `promote`, `implement`, `fix`).
  Per-commit Conventional Commit titles on the feature branch don't trip either rule — only the PR title (which becomes the squashed `main` commit) is gated.
- Linear auto-closes the linked SMA-* issue when its PR merges; no manual status move needed.
- **Always implement GitHub Actions against the latest stable major**, pinned to a commit SHA (never a moving `@vN` tag), keeping the human-readable version as a trailing `# vX.Y.Z` comment **on the `uses:` line**, so the SHA is auditable. The comment must end with the version: Dependabot updates only a same-line comment that ends with the old version, so a version on its own line above the step goes stale on every bump (SMA-744). This rule applies only to pins of a tagged release. `dtolnay/rust-toolchain` is pinned to an untagged `master` commit, so it has no version comment. Do not add one, because no tag gives a correct version. The `gh-actions` Dependabot group sets no `update-types`, so its configuration permits major bumps in the same grouped PR. Do not depend on that: `actions/checkout` still sat on v6.0.2 until SMA-486 bumped it by hand, so **check for a new major by hand**. `dtolnay/rust-toolchain` is a special case: it ships rolling branches and a periodically re-pointed `v1` tag, so confirm the direction (`ahead_by > 0, behind_by == 0`) before accepting any bump — the naive "bump to latest release" recipe once would have proposed an ~11-month downgrade. Independently and permanently: every site pinning it **must** pair the SHA with an explicit `with: toolchain: …`, because a SHA ref carries no toolchain selector. Recipes and history: `docs/runbooks/github-actions-pinning.md`.
- **After a PR merges to `main`, release-plz opens/updates a `chore: release` PR** (authored by the paigasusbot App) carrying the version bumps + CHANGELOG; in the normal flow **merging that PR is what publishes to crates.io** (the merged feature PR left versions matching the registry, so its own `main` push publishes nothing). The exception is a PR that bumps its own version — the stub-ascend ritual — which publishes on its own merge with no separate release PR. Check the release PR after every merge and watch its CI — its release-PR `cargo update` can pull a fresh advisory that reddens `audit`/`deny` on the bot PR **only** (independent of `main`); fix with a `chore(deps)` pin and release-plz regenerates the PR clean.

## CI

`.github/workflows/ci.yml` runs nine jobs on every PR (`commits` is PR-only; the other eight also run on push to `main`): `fmt`, `clippy`, `test` (matrix `{ubuntu, macos, windows} × {stable, 1.94}`, `fail-fast: false`), `build-no-default-features`, `docs` (`RUSTDOCFLAGS=-D warnings`), `doc-coverage` (gated at `DOC_COVERAGE_THRESHOLD`, default 80%), `commits` (`convco check`), `sessions-it` (Postgres/Redis, path-filtered), and `markdown-lint`. The `paigasus-helikon-cli` crate is excluded from both the `missing_docs` lint and the coverage aggregator until its public API stabilizes.

`.github/workflows/integration.yml` runs `temporal-it` and `agentcore-image` as **signal-only** jobs, deliberately outside `ci.yml` so an expected flake cannot make "ci is red on `main`" meaningless. **Signal-only means *not listed as required*, never `continue-on-error`.**

`.github/workflows/msrv.yml` runs `cargo msrv --path crates/paigasus-helikon-core verify` as a non-required signal that the declared MSRV is truthful.

Supply-chain workflows (`audit.yml`, `deny.yml`, `sbom.yml`) are separate from `ci.yml` because they have independent triggers and failure semantics. `audit.yml` and `deny.yml` both run on push to `main`, PRs, a daily cron, and `workflow_dispatch`, so `main` is re-evaluated daily at exactly PR severity.

**To read an audit verdict, use the Checks API, not the legacy commit-status API** — the latter returns only `CodeRabbit` on this repo, rendering a confident `state: success` that contains no audit verdict whatsoever:

```bash
gh api repos/SMK1085/paigasus-helikon/commits/main/check-runs \
  --jq '.check_runs[] | select(.name=="audit" or .name=="deny") | {name, status, conclusion}'
```

Note also that the `scheduled-audit` job's green status means nothing at any severity — read the *run* conclusion, never that job's status.

The required-status-check contexts gated on `main` are (bare job names, as posted by the GitHub Actions app): `fmt`, `clippy`, `test (ubuntu-latest, stable)`, `test (macos-latest, stable)`, `test (windows-latest, stable)`, `docs`, `doc-coverage`, `book-build`, `commits`, `pr-title`, `audit`, `deny`, `sessions-it`, `build-no-default-features`, `markdown-lint`. The macOS job is required because it is the only gate that compiles and runs the Seatbelt backend; the Windows job because it is the only gate that exercises the Windows timeout path in `paigasus-helikon-tools` — `cmd /C` process spawning and a `TerminateProcess`-based kill, which unlike the unix path has no process-group semantics and assigns a real exit code (SMA-569); `sessions-it` because it is the only gate that runs the live Postgres/Redis session backends; `build-no-default-features` because it is the only gate that compiles `runtime-axum` and `runtime-actix` with default features off. The canonical declaration is `.github/rulesets/main-protection-checks.json` (see CONTRIBUTING.md → "Repo configuration"). Other matrix variants (the `1.94` legs) run as signals only.

These pins are hand-bumped with nothing tracking them: `TEMPORAL_CLI_VERSION`/`TEMPORAL_CLI_SHA256` in `integration.yml`, `NIGHTLY_TOOLCHAIN` in `ci.yml`, `convco@…` in `ci.yml`'s `commits` job, `MDBOOK_VERSION`/`MDBOOK_LINKCHECK_VERSION` in `docs.yml`, and `markdownlint-cli2` via `package-lock.json`. **A checksum mismatch is never a signal to update the digest** — the causes are, in order, a truncated download, an upstream re-tag, and tampering; verify upstream independently first.

**The workspace needs no system `protoc`** (SMA-623): `temporalio-client`'s `vendored-protox` feature compiles the Temporal protos with `protox`. `ci.yml` sets `PROTOC` to a path that does not exist, and `build-no-default-features` asserts that the feature is active. If a build fails with "Could not find `protoc`", do not add a `protoc` install — find which build script calls it. Rationale and recovery: `docs/runbooks/ci-architecture.md` → "protoc and protox".

Job-by-job rationale, the audit/deny signal semantics, and the incident history behind all of the above: `docs/runbooks/ci-architecture.md`.

**GitHub's 10 GB Actions cache limit is a standing constraint, not a one-time cleanup** (SMA-618): it is GitHub's **default**, not a hard ceiling — a repo admin, org owner or enterprise owner can raise it (user-owned repos up to 10 TB) at additional storage cost, and SMA-618 deliberately chose to fit inside it rather than pay. Enforced at 10 **GiB** (10,737,418,240 bytes) despite the "10 GB" wording. Going over fails nothing — it just triggers silent LRU eviction that makes CI legs run cold at random. `cache-budget.yml` monitors it daily and warns (never fails) above 8.5 GiB. Caches are saved **only** from `main` (`save-if: ${{ github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' }}` on every `Swatinem/rust-cache` site) so a PR job can still restore an entry `main` wrote but never writes a competing `refs/pull/N/merge` entry that evicts it. The `CARGO_*`/`RUST*`-prefixed workflow env that `rust-cache` hashes into its key must stay byte-identical across every cache-bearing workflow, enforced by `scripts/check-cargo-profile-env-sync.sh` running as a step in `fmt`. `audit` and `deny` deliberately cache no `target/` directory — neither compiles the workspace, so it was pure waste against the fixed budget.  CI also sets **`CARGO_PROFILE_DEV_DEBUG: line-tables-only`** (SMA-618 PR 2), which measured a **16.5% cut in total cache bytes** — 14-29% on the `test` legs and exactly 0% on `clippy`/`docs`/`doc-coverage`, which are metadata-mode builds with no debug info to remove. (A local sample of the largest `.rlib` files suggested 79%; do not extrapolate an aggregate from its densest component.) Keeping line tables preserves file:line in panic backtraces. ## Local hooks

Hooks are managed via `cargo-husky` (user-hooks mode) and live in `.cargo-husky/hooks/`. They install into `.git/hooks/` on the next dev-dep realization of `paigasus-helikon`. To force a re-install after editing one: `rm -rf target/debug/build/cargo-husky-* && cargo test -p paigasus-helikon --no-run`.

- **`commit-msg`** — runs `convco check --from-stdin` (enforces the `.versionrc` allowlist).
- **`pre-commit`** — intentional no-op (`exit 0`). The file exists to claim the slot so future cargo-husky upgrades don't fill it in with surprise behavior.
- **`pre-push`** — runs `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-features --all-targets -- -D warnings`, and `convco check <merge-base>..HEAD`. Catches the three fastest CI gates pre-push; deliberately omits `cargo test` and `cargo doc` (too slow for every push). Bypass for WIP branches: `git push --no-verify`.

Three rules here are easy to get wrong, and each has already cost a debugging session:

- **The re-install silently does nothing inside a git worktree** — cargo-husky searches for a `.git` *directory* and a worktree's is a file, so it installs nothing and the old hook keeps running. Run the re-install from the **main checkout**, and verify with `grep` against the installed copy rather than assuming.
- **Never hand-copy a hook onto `.git/hooks/<name>`** — on this machine the Entire CLI owns `pre-push` and chains to `.git/hooks/pre-push.pre-entire`, which is where the cargo-husky hook actually lives. Check for a `.pre-entire` sibling first and install into that slot.
- **The convco baseline must be a merge-base, not a branch tip** — `convco check A..B` silently falls back to walking the entire history when `A` is not an ancestor of `B`, rejecting correct branches with failures the author did not write.

Mechanics and the SMA-547 postmortem: `docs/runbooks/local-hooks.md`.

## Fixture line endings

`.gitattributes` pins `crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-anthropic/tests/fixtures/*.txt` to `text eol=lf`. The streaming tests `include_str!` the SSE fixtures and split them on literal `\n` delimiters; without this, Windows checkouts produce CRLF bytes and the literal-string splits return one part instead of two. When adding wire-format fixtures elsewhere that the test code parses byte-level, extend the rule.

1	# SMA-804: Turn-boundary checkpoint on `RunContext`
2	
3	- Linear: [SMA-804](https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-804)
4	- ADR: Helikon ADR-15 "Deferred tool calls and a turn-boundary checkpoint", which implements ADR-0028 decision (h) in `paigasus-core`.
5	- Sibling: SMA-803 (deferred tool calls). It owns `StopReason`, `Deferred` and the terminal-event change.
6	- Status: draft for spec approval (GATE 1).
7	
8	## 1. Intent
9	
10	The always-on agent host runs Helikon's `TokioRunner`. Events can arrive while a run is in progress: a new inbox message, or an operator cancel from the console. Today the host has only two choices. It can wait for the run to end, or it can cancel the `CancellationToken`. A cancel can stop a tool call in the middle of its work. Nothing can add a user-role message to a run that is in progress.
11	
12	The host needs a safe point between turns. At that point it can do one of three things:
13	
14	- let the run continue,
15	- add user content (the `fold` and `interrupt` policies), or
16	- stop the run cleanly (the operator cancel).
17	
18	"Cleanly" means that no tool call is half done, and that the session history stays valid for replay.
19	
20	## 2. Goals, non-goals, anti-goals
21	
22	**Goals**
23	
24	- G1. An optional callback on `RunContext`. The loop calls it at every turn boundary of the top-level loop and of handoff children.
25	- G2. The callback returns `Continue`, `Inject(Vec<ContentPart>)` or `Stop { reason }`.
26	- G3. Injected content is user content. The loop emits a new `AgentEvent` for it, and `SessionRecorder` stores it as a `SessionEvent::UserMessage`. The next model call and the stored history both contain it.
27	- G4. The input guardrails check injected content. A tripwire stops the run with `StopReason::Stopped`.
28	- G5. `Stop` ends the run at the boundary with `StopReason::Stopped { reason }`. No tool call is half done.
29	- G6. The change is compile-compatible for callers. The field is optional, and all new types are `#[non_exhaustive]`.
30	
31	**Non-goals**
32	
33	- N1. `TemporalRunner`. Its `DurableDriver` does not use the caller's `RunContext`, so the callback never fires there. A workflow-signal form is a later issue (ADR-15, Consequences).
34	- N2. Workflow, swarm and graph sub-agents (`subagent_child`). The callback does not fire in these sub-agents. The decision is in section 4, D2.
35	- N3. `AgentAsTool` sub-runs. The callback never fires there.
36	- N4. A checkpoint inside a tool call, or before the first model call of a run.
37	- N5. A host-side `fold` or `interrupt` policy. The host builds these on top of this callback.
38	
39	**Anti-goals** (the result is a failure even if it compiles)
40	
41	- A1. An injected user message sits between a tool call and its tool result in the event stream or in the stored session. Replay then fails at the provider.
42	- A2. A `Stop` leaves a tool call without a result, or it shows as a run failure (`RunFailed`).
43	- A3. The loop records injected content that the model never sees, and the run then ends. The host loses an event that it could keep in its inbox.
44	- A4. One `Inject` reaches more than one concurrent loop.
45	
46	## 3. Constraints
47	
48	- C1. **SMA-803 lands first.** SMA-803 adds `StopReason` and the field `RunResult::stop_reason`. It also makes the terminal event carry the stop reason, so that `run_streamed` consumers see it. The two sessions agreed on this shape:
49	  `#[non_exhaustive] pub enum StopReason { Completed, Deferred { calls: Vec<PendingToolCall> }, Stopped { reason: String } }`.
50	  SMA-804 rebases on SMA-803 and uses its terminal-event mechanism. SMA-803 might not be on `main` when SMA-804 is ready. In that case, SMA-804 adds the enum with `Completed` and `Stopped` only, plus the field. SMA-803 then adds `Deferred`.
51	- C2. **"No call at a deferred boundary"** follows from SMA-803. A turn with a deferred call ends the run at that boundary, so the loop never reaches the checkpoint. SMA-804 adds a test for this after the rebase.
52	- C3. `RunContext` has no `Clone`. Each child-context site lists every field by hand: `handoff_child`, `subagent_child`, `to_tool_context`, the `AgentAsTool` rebuild, and `runtime-temporal`'s `WorkerPosture::apply`. Each site needs an explicit decision for the new field (section 6.3).
53	- C4. Workspace MSRV is 1.94. Core already uses `async_trait`-style object-safe async traits for `ApprovalHandler`, so the new trait uses the same form.
54	- C5. Release: this is an additive `feat` in `paigasus-helikon-core`, so release-plz makes a patch bump. There is no hand bump, unless the core-API-in-the-same-PR rule in `CLAUDE.md` applies.
55	
56	## 4. Decisions made with Sven
57	
58	- **D1. Approach A: a trait object on `RunContext`.** `TurnCheckpoint<Ctx>` is an object-safe async trait, set with `RunContext::with_turn_checkpoint(Arc<dyn TurnCheckpoint<Ctx>>)`. It uses the same pattern as `ApprovalHandler`.
59	- **D2. Scope (a): only the top-level loop and handoff children.** `handoff_child` copies the field. `subagent_child` sets it to `None`. If the root agent is a workflow agent, the callback never fires. This is accepted for v1.
60	
61	### Approaches that we considered
62	
63	| | Approach | Trade-off | Result |
64	|---|---|---|---|
65	| A | `Arc<dyn TurnCheckpoint<Ctx>>` on `RunContext` | Same pattern as `ApprovalHandler`. Can get new default methods later. | **Chosen** |
66	| B | Boxed closure `Arc<dyn Fn(TurnBoundary) -> BoxFuture<'static, CheckpointDecision>>` | Easy to write in tests. The future cannot borrow the context, it is hard to extend, and no other core callback uses this form. | Rejected |
67	| C | New `HookEvent::OnTurnBoundary` plus `HookDecision::{InjectUserMessage, Stop}` | Reuses the hook registry. Hooks have many subscribers, so it needs merge rules, and each new decision needs a meaning at the seven other hook points. Does not match "one callback on `RunContext`". | Rejected |
68	
69	## 5. The design
70	
71	### 5.1 Public API (`paigasus-helikon-core`)
72	
73	```rust
74	/// Where the loop is when it calls the checkpoint.
75	#[non_exhaustive]
76	#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
77	pub struct TurnBoundary {
78	    /// The turn whose tool results were just recorded (0-based).
79	    pub completed_turn: u32,
80	    /// The turn the next model call will start.
81	    pub next_turn: u32,
82	    /// The name of the agent whose loop is at the boundary (the handoff target in a child).
83	    pub agent: String,
84	    /// `RunContext::agent_depth()` of that loop.
85	    pub depth: u32,
86	}
87	
88	/// What the loop does after the checkpoint.
89	#[non_exhaustive]
90	#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq)]
91	pub enum CheckpointDecision {
92	    /// Call the model as normal.
93	    Continue,
94	    /// Add these parts as one user message, then call the model.
95	    Inject(Vec<ContentPart>),
96	    /// End the run here with `StopReason::Stopped { reason }`.
97	    Stop { reason: String },
98	}
99	
100	#[async_trait]
101	pub trait TurnCheckpoint<Ctx>: Send + Sync
102	where
103	    Ctx: Send + Sync + 'static,
104	{
105	    async fn at_boundary(&self, ctx: &RunContext<Ctx>, boundary: &TurnBoundary) -> CheckpointDecision;
106	}
107	```
108	
109	On `RunContext`:
110	
111	- the field `turn_checkpoint: Option<Arc<dyn TurnCheckpoint<Ctx>>>` (private, default `None`),
112	- `pub fn with_turn_checkpoint(self, cp: Arc<dyn TurnCheckpoint<Ctx>>) -> Self`,
113	- `pub fn turn_checkpoint(&self) -> Option<&Arc<dyn TurnCheckpoint<Ctx>>>`.
114	
115	A new `AgentEvent` variant (not terminal, so `is_terminal()` stays `false` for it):
116	
117	```rust
118	/// User content that the turn-boundary checkpoint added to the run.
119	UserMessageInjected { content: Vec<ContentPart> },
120	```
121	
122	The exact names are the builder's call within these semantics (ADR-0028 §8). The names above are the proposal.
123	
124	### 5.2 Where the loop calls it
125	
126	A **turn boundary** is the transition `ExecutingTools → CallingModel { turn: n }`. That is the point after the tool results of turn `n-1` are recorded and before the model call of turn `n`.
127	
128	Required event order at a boundary:
129	
130	```text
131	ToolCallItem…  (turn n-1)
132	ToolOutputItem… (all results of turn n-1)      ← emitted by transition()
133	[checkpoint runs here]
134	UserMessageInjected { content }                ← only on Inject
135	TurnStarted { turn: n }
136	TokenDelta… / MessageOutput… (turn n)
137	```
138	
139	The `ToolOutputItem` events come from the *next* `transition()` call, not from the `ExecuteTools` arm in `agent.rs`. So the checkpoint must **not** run in the `ExecuteTools` arm. If it did, `UserMessageInjected` would come before the tool results. `SessionRecorder` would then store a user message between a tool call and its result (anti-goal A1).
140	
141	Proposed mechanism (the builder can choose another one that keeps the order above):
142	
143	- In the driver's event loop, find the case where the previous state was `ExecutingTools` and `next_action` is `CallModel`.
144	- Yield the `ToolOutputItem` events. Then, before the driver handles `TurnStarted { n }` (the turn span and the `OnTurnStart` hook), call the checkpoint if one is set.
145	- On `Continue`, proceed as today.
146	- On `Inject(parts)`:
147	  1. Run the guardrails (5.4).
148	  2. Yield `UserMessageInjected { content: parts }`.
149	  3. Push `Item::UserMessage { content: parts }` to `conversation`.
150	  4. Append the same item to the `ModelRequest.messages` that `transition()` already built. The request was built from the conversation before the push, so this append is necessary.
151	  5. Then handle `TurnStarted { n }` and call the model.
152	- On `Stop { reason }`: end the run (5.5). Do not yield `TurnStarted { n }`, do not fire `OnTurnStart`, and do not call the model.
153	
154	Other rules:
155	
156	- **Max turns.** `transition()` checks `next_turn >= max_turns` before it produces `CallModel`. In that case it emits `RunFailed`, and the loop never reaches the checkpoint. So the callback does not run when the next turn would exceed `max_turns` (anti-goal A3). This is the intended behaviour, and a test locks it in.
157	- **The first model call** (turn 0) is not a boundary. There are no tool results before it, and the input guardrails already ran on the seed input.
158	- **A turn that ends in a handoff** is not a boundary in the parent. The handoff child runs its own loop, and that loop has its own boundaries.
159	- **A turn with a final answer** (no tool calls) ends the run. It is not a boundary.
160	- **The `CallingModel` max-turns check** (`loop_state.rs:230`) is unchanged.
161	
162	### 5.3 `Inject` details
163	
164	- One `Inject` makes exactly one user message (one `Item::UserMessage`, one event, one `SessionEvent::UserMessage`).
165	- `Inject(vec![])` (an empty list) is treated as `Continue`. No event is emitted and no message is pushed. *(My call.)*
166	- The loop does not inspect or filter the parts. The doc comment says that callers should send user parts (`Text`, `Image`, `Audio`). Tool parts in a user message are the caller's error, and the loop does not check for them. *(My call.)*
167	- `SessionRecorder::observe` gets one new arm: `UserMessageInjected { content }` maps to `SessionEvent::user_message(content)`. Then `project()` returns it as `Item::UserMessage` on the next run, with no new `SessionEvent` variant. So no session backend changes.
168	- Pending `OnTurnStart` hook injections (`pending_injections`, request-only `Item::System`) keep their current behaviour. They are added to the request after the injected user message, because the request is built first and the hook fires at `TurnStarted`.
169	
170	### 5.4 Guardrails on injected content
171	
172	- The loop calls the existing `interceptors.run_input_guardrails(text)`. `text` joins the `Text` parts of the injected content, with the same join rule as `user_text_of`.
173	- The guardrails run even if there is no `Text` part (`text` is then `""`). This matches the seed-input path, which also always runs. A guardrail cannot check image or audio parts, because `GuardrailInput` has only `UserText`. This is a known limit, and the doc comment says so.
174	- On a tripwire:
175	  1. Yield `GuardrailTriggered { kind, info }`.
176	  2. Do **not** yield `UserMessageInjected`, do not push to the conversation, and do not record the content. Content that a guardrail rejected must not reach the model or the stored history. *(My call.)*
177	  3. End the run as for `Stop` (5.5), with `reason = "input guardrail tripwire"`.
178	- The issue requires `Stop`, so a tripwire ends with `StopReason::Stopped` and **not** with `RunFailed` / `AgentError::Guardrail`. This is different from a tripwire on the seed input, which stays a failure. A host can tell the two kinds of stop apart: the `GuardrailTriggered` event comes just before the terminal event.
179	
180	### 5.5 `Stop` details
181	
182	- `Stop` ends the run with a **successful** terminal event that carries `StopReason::Stopped { reason }`. This uses the mechanism from SMA-803. It is not `RunFailed`, and the `FailureSlot` stays empty (anti-goal A2).
183	- `RunResultStreaming::collect()` returns `Ok(RunResult { stop_reason: Stopped { reason }, .. })`.
184	- `final_output` follows the normal `collect` rule: the text of the last `MessageOutput`. This can be the text that came with the tool calls of turn `n-1`, or `""`. The `final_output` of a run that did not complete uses the same rule as for `Deferred` (SMA-803). SMA-804 follows whatever SMA-803 decides for `collect_typed` and `parse_final` on a run that did not complete.
185	- `usage` covers every turn that ran.
186	- `OnRunComplete` fires, the same as at any other clean end (`NextAction::Terminate`). *(My call.)*
187	- **Handoff child.** A `Stop` in a handoff child ends the child loop. The parent re-yields the child's events and then returns, so the whole run ends with `Stopped`. The parent's handoff code must pass the stop reason through, and it must not replace it with `Completed`. The rebase on SMA-803 has to check this path.
188	- The tool calls of turn `n-1` all have results before the checkpoint runs, so a `Stop` cannot leave a tool call half done. `SessionRecorder::drain` therefore has no orphan `ToolCalled` to fix.
189	
190	### 5.6 Cancellation
191	
192	The loop does not poll the `CancellationToken`. `TokioRunner::controlled()` drops the stream when a cancel or a timeout happens. If the stream is dropped while `at_boundary` waits, the callback's future is dropped too. The trait doc says that `at_boundary` must be cancel-safe. The host can also use `ctx.cancel()` inside the callback.
193	
194	## 6. Change map
195	
196	### 6.1 `paigasus-helikon-core`
197	
198	- A new module, for example `src/checkpoint.rs`, with `TurnBoundary`, `CheckpointDecision` and `TurnCheckpoint`. Re-export these at the crate root, with `///` docs on every public item.
199	- `src/context.rs`: the field, the builder, the getter, and the child sites (6.3).
200	- `src/agent.rs`:
201	  - the boundary hook in the driver (5.2),
202	  - the new `AgentEvent` variant,
203	  - the `terminal_tests` update (the wildcard-free `classify`, `every_variant()`, and the variant count).
204	- `src/session.rs`: the `observe` arm, and a recorder unit test.
205	- Tests and snapshots: `tests/serde_roundtrip.rs` plus a new snapshot for `UserMessageInjected`. Also check that `tests/loop_happy_path.rs` (`event_kind`) still compiles.
206	
207	### 6.2 Other crates
208	
209	- `runtime-agentcore/src/agui/map.rs`: map `UserMessageInjected`. The proposal is an AG-UI custom event, for example `helikon.user_message_injected`, in the same style as `helikon.approval`. If the match has a wildcard, still add an explicit arm, so the event is not lost silently. *(My call.)*
210	- The other matches outside core (`runtime-axum` dto/event_log/registry, `evals` trajectory, `cli` repl) have wildcards because the enum is `#[non_exhaustive]`. The builder checks each one and adds an arm only where the event has a meaning (for example, the CLI REPL can print it).
211	- `runtime-temporal`: no code change. Add a doc note on `TemporalRunner` / `WorkerPosture` that the turn checkpoint is not supported (N1).
212	
213	### 6.3 Child-context sites
214	
215	| Site | New field |
216	|---|---|
217	| `RunContext::handoff_child` | copy (`Arc` clone) |
218	| `RunContext::subagent_child` | `None` (D2) |
219	| `RunContext::to_tool_context` | not carried (`ToolContext` has no field for it) |
220	| `AgentAsTool` sub-context rebuild | not set (N3), so it is `None` because `RunContext::new` sets `None` |
221	| `runtime-temporal` `WorkerPosture::apply` | not copied (N1). Its field-enumeration test does not change, because this is not a posture field. |
222	
223	### 6.4 Documentation
224	
225	- The mdBook (`docs/book/src/`): the page that describes the run loop or `RunContext` gets a section "Turn-boundary checkpoint". The section covers the three decisions, the event order, the guardrail rule, the max-turns rule, and the non-goals (Temporal, workflow sub-agents, `AgentAsTool`).
226	- `crates/paigasus-helikon-core/README.md`: add one line or a short example only if the README lists `RunContext` capabilities. The builder checks this. The facade and root READMEs do not change, because the crate roster and the features do not change.
227	- The core `CHANGELOG.md` is written by release-plz from the commit messages. No hand edit is necessary.
228	
229	## 7. Tests (the "Done when" list)
230	
231	All tests are in `paigasus-helikon-core/tests/` and use `common::MockModel`, `MockTool` and a recording model (the same as `injection.rs`). A test checkpoint returns scripted decisions and records each `TurnBoundary` that it gets.
232	
233	1. **Continue.** Script: tool call, then a final answer. The checkpoint is called once, with `completed_turn = 0` and `next_turn = 1`. The run completes, and the event stream is the same as with no checkpoint.
234	2. **Inject.**
235	   - The model request of turn 1 ends with `Item::UserMessage { injected parts }`, after the `ToolResult`.
236	   - The event order is exactly: `ToolOutputItem`, `UserMessageInjected`, `TurnStarted { 1 }`.
237	   - `SessionRecorder` gives `…ToolReturned, UserMessage(injected)…`, and `project()` round-trips it.
238	   - A `runtime-tokio` test with a counting session shows that the stored session holds the injected `UserMessage` after the `ToolReturned`.
239	3. **Inject with empty parts** behaves as `Continue`.
240	4. **Stop.**
241	   - `collect()` returns `Ok` with `StopReason::Stopped { reason }`.

243	   - Every `ToolCalled` has a `ToolReturned`.

# SMA-804: Turn-boundary checkpoint on `RunContext`

- Linear: [SMA-804](https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-804)
- ADR: Helikon ADR-15 "Deferred tool calls and a turn-boundary checkpoint", which implements ADR-0028 decision (h) in `paigasus-core`.
- Sibling: SMA-803 (deferred tool calls). It owns `StopReason`, `Deferred` and the terminal-event change.
- Status: draft for spec approval (GATE 1).

## 1. Intent

The always-on agent host runs Helikon's `TokioRunner`. Events can arrive while a run is in progress: a new inbox message, or an operator cancel from the console. Today the host has only two choices. It can wait for the run to end, or it can cancel the `CancellationToken`. A cancel can stop a tool call in the middle of its work. Nothing can add a user-role message to a run that is in progress.

The host needs a safe point between turns. At that point it can do one of three things:

- let the run continue,
- add user content (the `fold` and `interrupt` policies), or
- stop the run cleanly (the operator cancel).

"Cleanly" means that no tool call is half done, and that the session history stays valid for replay.

## 2. Goals, non-goals, anti-goals

**Goals**

- G1. An optional callback on `RunContext`. The loop calls it at every turn boundary of the top-level loop and of handoff children.
- G2. The callback returns `Continue`, `Inject(Vec<ContentPart>)` or `Stop { reason }`.
- G3. Injected content is user content. The loop emits a new `AgentEvent` for it, and `SessionRecorder` stores it as a `SessionEvent::UserMessage`. The next model call and the stored history both contain it.
- G4. The input guardrails check injected content. A tripwire stops the run with `StopReason::Stopped`.
- G5. `Stop` ends the run at the boundary with `StopReason::Stopped { reason }`. No tool call is half done.
- G6. The change is compile-compatible for callers. The field is optional, and all new types are `#[non_exhaustive]`.

**Non-goals**

- N1. `TemporalRunner`. Its `DurableDriver` does not use the caller's `RunContext`, so the callback never fires there. A workflow-signal form is a later issue (ADR-15, Consequences).
- N2. Workflow, swarm and graph sub-agents (`subagent_child`). The callback does not fire in these sub-agents. The decision is in section 4, D2.
- N3. `AgentAsTool` sub-runs. The callback never fires there.
- N4. A checkpoint inside a tool call, or before the first model call of a run.
- N5. A host-side `fold` or `interrupt` policy. The host builds these on top of this callback.

**Anti-goals** (the result is a failure even if it compiles)

- A1. An injected user message sits between a tool call and its tool result in the event stream or in the stored session. Replay then fails at the provider.
- A2. A `Stop` leaves a tool call without a result, or it shows as a run failure (`RunFailed`).
- A3. The loop records injected content that the model never sees, and the run then ends. The host loses an event that it could keep in its inbox.
- A4. One `Inject` reaches more than one concurrent loop.

## 3. Constraints

- C1. **SMA-803 lands first.** SMA-803 adds `StopReason` and the field `RunResult::stop_reason`. It also makes the terminal event carry the stop reason, so that `run_streamed` consumers see it. The two sessions agreed on this shape:
  `#[non_exhaustive] pub enum StopReason { Completed, Deferred { calls: Vec<PendingToolCall> }, Stopped { reason: String } }`.
  SMA-804 rebases on SMA-803 and uses its terminal-event mechanism. SMA-803 might not be on `main` when SMA-804 is ready. In that case, SMA-804 adds the enum with `Completed` and `Stopped` only, plus the field. SMA-803 then adds `Deferred`.
- C2. **"No call at a deferred boundary"** follows from SMA-803. A turn with a deferred call ends the run at that boundary, so the loop never reaches the checkpoint. SMA-804 adds a test for this after the rebase.
- C3. `RunContext` has no `Clone`. Each child-context site lists every field by hand: `handoff_child`, `subagent_child`, `to_tool_context`, the `AgentAsTool` rebuild, and `runtime-temporal`'s `WorkerPosture::apply`. Each site needs an explicit decision for the new field (section 6.3).
- C4. Workspace MSRV is 1.94. Core already uses `async_trait`-style object-safe async traits for `ApprovalHandler`, so the new trait uses the same form.
- C5. Release: this is an additive `feat` in `paigasus-helikon-core`, so release-plz makes a patch bump. There is no hand bump, unless the core-API-in-the-same-PR rule in `CLAUDE.md` applies.

## 4. Decisions made with Sven

- **D1. Approach A: a trait object on `RunContext`.** `TurnCheckpoint<Ctx>` is an object-safe async trait, set with `RunContext::with_turn_checkpoint(Arc<dyn TurnCheckpoint<Ctx>>)`. It uses the same pattern as `ApprovalHandler`.
- **D2. Scope (a): only the top-level loop and handoff children.** `handoff_child` copies the field. `subagent_child` sets it to `None`. If the root agent is a workflow agent, the callback never fires. This is accepted for v1.

### Approaches that we considered

| | Approach | Trade-off | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| A | `Arc<dyn TurnCheckpoint<Ctx>>` on `RunContext` | Same pattern as `ApprovalHandler`. Can get new default methods later. | **Chosen** |
| B | Boxed closure `Arc<dyn Fn(TurnBoundary) -> BoxFuture<'static, CheckpointDecision>>` | Easy to write in tests. The future cannot borrow the context, it is hard to extend, and no other core callback uses this form. | Rejected |
| C | New `HookEvent::OnTurnBoundary` plus `HookDecision::{InjectUserMessage, Stop}` | Reuses the hook registry. Hooks have many subscribers, so it needs merge rules, and each new decision needs a meaning at the seven other hook points. Does not match "one callback on `RunContext`". | Rejected |

## 5. The design

### 5.1 Public API (`paigasus-helikon-core`)

```rust
/// Where the loop is when it calls the checkpoint.
#[non_exhaustive]
#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct TurnBoundary {
    /// The turn whose tool results were just recorded (0-based).
    pub completed_turn: u32,
    /// The turn the next model call will start.
    pub next_turn: u32,
    /// The name of the agent whose loop is at the boundary (the handoff target in a child).
    pub agent: String,
    /// `RunContext::agent_depth()` of that loop.
    pub depth: u32,
}

/// What the loop does after the checkpoint.
#[non_exhaustive]
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq)]
pub enum CheckpointDecision {
    /// Call the model as normal.
    Continue,
    /// Add these parts as one user message, then call the model.
    Inject(Vec<ContentPart>),
    /// End the run here with `StopReason::Stopped { reason }`.
    Stop { reason: String },
}

#[async_trait]
pub trait TurnCheckpoint<Ctx>: Send + Sync
where
    Ctx: Send + Sync + 'static,
{
    async fn at_boundary(&self, ctx: &RunContext<Ctx>, boundary: &TurnBoundary) -> CheckpointDecision;
}
```

On `RunContext`:

- the field `turn_checkpoint: Option<Arc<dyn TurnCheckpoint<Ctx>>>` (private, default `None`),
- `pub fn with_turn_checkpoint(self, cp: Arc<dyn TurnCheckpoint<Ctx>>) -> Self`,
- `pub fn turn_checkpoint(&self) -> Option<&Arc<dyn TurnCheckpoint<Ctx>>>`.

A new `AgentEvent` variant (not terminal, so `is_terminal()` stays `false` for it):

```rust
/// User content that the turn-boundary checkpoint added to the run.
UserMessageInjected { content: Vec<ContentPart> },
```

The exact names are the builder's call within these semantics (ADR-0028 §8). The names above are the proposal.

### 5.2 Where the loop calls it

A **turn boundary** is the transition `ExecutingTools → CallingModel { turn: n }`. That is the point after the tool results of turn `n-1` are recorded and before the model call of turn `n`.

Required event order at a boundary:

```text
ToolCallItem…  (turn n-1)
ToolOutputItem… (all results of turn n-1)      ← emitted by transition()
[checkpoint runs here]
UserMessageInjected { content }                ← only on Inject
TurnStarted { turn: n }
TokenDelta… / MessageOutput… (turn n)
```

The `ToolOutputItem` events come from the *next* `transition()` call, not from the `ExecuteTools` arm in `agent.rs`. So the checkpoint must **not** run in the `ExecuteTools` arm. If it did, `UserMessageInjected` would come before the tool results. `SessionRecorder` would then store a user message between a tool call and its result (anti-goal A1).

Proposed mechanism (the builder can choose another one that keeps the order above):

- In the driver's event loop, find the case where the previous state was `ExecutingTools` and `next_action` is `CallModel`.
- Yield the `ToolOutputItem` events. Then, before the driver handles `TurnStarted { n }` (the turn span and the `OnTurnStart` hook), call the checkpoint if one is set.
- On `Continue`, proceed as today.
- On `Inject(parts)`:
  1. Run the guardrails (5.4).
  2. Yield `UserMessageInjected { content: parts }`.
  3. Push `Item::UserMessage { content: parts }` to `conversation`.
  4. Append the same item to the `ModelRequest.messages` that `transition()` already built. The request was built from the conversation before the push, so this append is necessary.
  5. Then handle `TurnStarted { n }` and call the model.
- On `Stop { reason }`: end the run (5.5). Do not yield `TurnStarted { n }`, do not fire `OnTurnStart`, and do not call the model.

Other rules:

- **Max turns.** `transition()` checks `next_turn >= max_turns` before it produces `CallModel`. In that case it emits `RunFailed`, and the loop never reaches the checkpoint. So the callback does not run when the next turn would exceed `max_turns` (anti-goal A3). This is the intended behaviour, and a test locks it in.
- **The first model call** (turn 0) is not a boundary. There are no tool results before it, and the input guardrails already ran on the seed input.
- **A turn that ends in a handoff** is not a boundary in the parent. The handoff child runs its own loop, and that loop has its own boundaries.
- **A turn with a final answer** (no tool calls) ends the run. It is not a boundary.
- **The `CallingModel` max-turns check** (`loop_state.rs:230`) is unchanged.

### 5.3 `Inject` details

- One `Inject` makes exactly one user message (one `Item::UserMessage`, one event, one `SessionEvent::UserMessage`).
- `Inject(vec![])` (an empty list) is treated as `Continue`. No event is emitted and no message is pushed. *(My call.)*
- The loop does not inspect or filter the parts. The doc comment says that callers should send user parts (`Text`, `Image`, `Audio`). Tool parts in a user message are the caller's error, and the loop does not check for them. *(My call.)*
- `SessionRecorder::observe` gets one new arm: `UserMessageInjected { content }` maps to `SessionEvent::user_message(content)`. Then `project()` returns it as `Item::UserMessage` on the next run, with no new `SessionEvent` variant. So no session backend changes.
- Pending `OnTurnStart` hook injections (`pending_injections`, request-only `Item::System`) keep their current behaviour. They are added to the request after the injected user message, because the request is built first and the hook fires at `TurnStarted`.

### 5.4 Guardrails on injected content

- The loop calls the existing `interceptors.run_input_guardrails(text)`. `text` joins the `Text` parts of the injected content, with the same join rule as `user_text_of`.
- The guardrails run even if there is no `Text` part (`text` is then `""`). This matches the seed-input path, which also always runs. A guardrail cannot check image or audio parts, because `GuardrailInput` has only `UserText`. This is a known limit, and the doc comment says so.
- On a tripwire:
  1. Yield `GuardrailTriggered { kind, info }`.
  2. Do **not** yield `UserMessageInjected`, do not push to the conversation, and do not record the content. Content that a guardrail rejected must not reach the model or the stored history. *(My call.)*
  3. End the run as for `Stop` (5.5), with `reason = "input guardrail tripwire"`.
- The issue requires `Stop`, so a tripwire ends with `StopReason::Stopped` and **not** with `RunFailed` / `AgentError::Guardrail`. This is different from a tripwire on the seed input, which stays a failure. A host can tell the two kinds of stop apart: the `GuardrailTriggered` event comes just before the terminal event.

### 5.5 `Stop` details

- `Stop` ends the run with a **successful** terminal event that carries `StopReason::Stopped { reason }`. This uses the mechanism from SMA-803. It is not `RunFailed`, and the `FailureSlot` stays empty (anti-goal A2).
- `RunResultStreaming::collect()` returns `Ok(RunResult { stop_reason: Stopped { reason }, .. })`.
- `final_output` follows the normal `collect` rule: the text of the last `MessageOutput`. This can be the text that came with the tool calls of turn `n-1`, or `""`. The `final_output` of a run that did not complete uses the same rule as for `Deferred` (SMA-803). SMA-804 follows whatever SMA-803 decides for `collect_typed` and `parse_final` on a run that did not complete.
- `usage` covers every turn that ran.
- `OnRunComplete` fires, the same as at any other clean end (`NextAction::Terminate`). *(My call.)*
- **Handoff child.** A `Stop` in a handoff child ends the child loop. The parent re-yields the child's events and then returns, so the whole run ends with `Stopped`. The parent's handoff code must pass the stop reason through, and it must not replace it with `Completed`. The rebase on SMA-803 has to check this path.
- The tool calls of turn `n-1` all have results before the checkpoint runs, so a `Stop` cannot leave a tool call half done. `SessionRecorder::drain` therefore has no orphan `ToolCalled` to fix.

### 5.6 Cancellation

The loop does not poll the `CancellationToken`. `TokioRunner::controlled()` drops the stream when a cancel or a timeout happens. If the stream is dropped while `at_boundary` waits, the callback's future is dropped too. The trait doc says that `at_boundary` must be cancel-safe. The host can also use `ctx.cancel()` inside the callback.

## 6. Change map

### 6.1 `paigasus-helikon-core`

- A new module, for example `src/checkpoint.rs`, with `TurnBoundary`, `CheckpointDecision` and `TurnCheckpoint`. Re-export these at the crate root, with `///` docs on every public item.
- `src/context.rs`: the field, the builder, the getter, and the child sites (6.3).
- `src/agent.rs`:
  - the boundary hook in the driver (5.2),
  - the new `AgentEvent` variant,
  - the `terminal_tests` update (the wildcard-free `classify`, `every_variant()`, and the variant count).
- `src/session.rs`: the `observe` arm, and a recorder unit test.
- Tests and snapshots: `tests/serde_roundtrip.rs` plus a new snapshot for `UserMessageInjected`. Also check that `tests/loop_happy_path.rs` (`event_kind`) still compiles.

### 6.2 Other crates

- `runtime-agentcore/src/agui/map.rs`: map `UserMessageInjected`. The proposal is an AG-UI custom event, for example `helikon.user_message_injected`, in the same style as `helikon.approval`. If the match has a wildcard, still add an explicit arm, so the event is not lost silently. *(My call.)*
- The other matches outside core (`runtime-axum` dto/event_log/registry, `evals` trajectory, `cli` repl) have wildcards because the enum is `#[non_exhaustive]`. The builder checks each one and adds an arm only where the event has a meaning (for example, the CLI REPL can print it).
- `runtime-temporal`: no code change. Add a doc note on `TemporalRunner` / `WorkerPosture` that the turn checkpoint is not supported (N1).

### 6.3 Child-context sites

| Site | New field |
|---|---|
| `RunContext::handoff_child` | copy (`Arc` clone) |
| `RunContext::subagent_child` | `None` (D2) |
| `RunContext::to_tool_context` | not carried (`ToolContext` has no field for it) |
| `AgentAsTool` sub-context rebuild | not set (N3), so it is `None` because `RunContext::new` sets `None` |
| `runtime-temporal` `WorkerPosture::apply` | not copied (N1). Its field-enumeration test does not change, because this is not a posture field. |

### 6.4 Documentation

- The mdBook (`docs/book/src/`): the page that describes the run loop or `RunContext` gets a section "Turn-boundary checkpoint". The section covers the three decisions, the event order, the guardrail rule, the max-turns rule, and the non-goals (Temporal, workflow sub-agents, `AgentAsTool`).
- `crates/paigasus-helikon-core/README.md`: add one line or a short example only if the README lists `RunContext` capabilities. The builder checks this. The facade and root READMEs do not change, because the crate roster and the features do not change.
- The core `CHANGELOG.md` is written by release-plz from the commit messages. No hand edit is necessary.

## 7. Tests (the "Done when" list)

All tests are in `paigasus-helikon-core/tests/` and use `common::MockModel`, `MockTool` and a recording model (the same as `injection.rs`). A test checkpoint returns scripted decisions and records each `TurnBoundary` that it gets.

1. **Continue.** Script: tool call, then a final answer. The checkpoint is called once, with `completed_turn = 0` and `next_turn = 1`. The run completes, and the event stream is the same as with no checkpoint.
2. **Inject.**
   - The model request of turn 1 ends with `Item::UserMessage { injected parts }`, after the `ToolResult`.
   - The event order is exactly: `ToolOutputItem`, `UserMessageInjected`, `TurnStarted { 1 }`.
   - `SessionRecorder` gives `…ToolReturned, UserMessage(injected)…`, and `project()` round-trips it.
   - A `runtime-tokio` test with a counting session shows that the stored session holds the injected `UserMessage` after the `ToolReturned`.
3. **Inject with empty parts** behaves as `Continue`.
4. **Stop.**
   - `collect()` returns `Ok` with `StopReason::Stopped { reason }`.
   - There is no second model call, no `TurnStarted { 1 }`, no `RunFailed`, and the `FailureSlot` is empty.
   - Every `ToolCalled` has a `ToolReturned`.
5. **Guardrail tripwire on injected content.**
   - A guardrail trips on the injected text. The stream has `GuardrailTriggered` and no `UserMessageInjected`.
   - The result is `Stopped` with the tripwire reason. There is no second model call, and the content is not in the recorder output.
6. **Max turns.** With `max_turns = 1` and a tool call on turn 0, the checkpoint is never called, and the run fails with `MaxTurnsExceeded` as today.
7. **Handoff child.** The checkpoint fires at a boundary inside the handoff target, with `agent = target` and `depth = 1`. A `Stop` there ends the whole run with `Stopped`.
8. **No call in an `AgentAsTool` sub-run.** The parent has a checkpoint, and the sub-agent makes a tool call inside its own loop. The checkpoint records only the parent's boundaries.
9. **No call in workflow sub-agents.** A `SequentialAgent` root with an `LlmAgent` child that uses tools: the checkpoint is never called. Also a unit test that `subagent_child()` has no checkpoint and `handoff_child()` has the same `Arc` (`Arc::ptr_eq`).
10. **No call at a deferred boundary** (after the rebase on SMA-803). A turn with one deferred call ends with `Deferred`, and the checkpoint is never called.
11. `AgentEvent` serde round trip, the snapshot, and the updated `terminal_tests` (`UserMessageInjected` is not terminal).

The CI gates in `CLAUDE.md` must pass: fmt, clippy `-D warnings`, `cargo test --workspace --all-features`, docs `-D warnings`, doc coverage, and `mdbook build docs/book`.

## 8. Left to the builder

- The exact names (trait, method, event, builder), within the semantics above.
- The exact way to place the hook in the driver, provided the event order in 5.2 holds.
- Whether `TurnBoundary` gets more fields (for example, the tool call ids of the completed turn). It is `#[non_exhaustive]`, so fields can be added later.
- The exact AG-UI event name.

## 9. Calls I made (please check)

1. The callback does not run when the next turn would exceed `max_turns` (5.2).
2. `Inject(vec![])` is `Continue` (5.3).
3. The loop does not filter tool parts in injected content (5.3).
4. On a guardrail tripwire, the injected content is not recorded anywhere (5.4).
5. The guardrails run even when the injected content has no text (5.4).
6. `OnRunComplete` fires on `Stop` (5.5).
7. The AG-UI mapper gets an explicit custom event (6.2).

review. This server wraps the official bioRxiv API to provide structured access
to preprint metadata, abstracts, and full-text PDFs.

• search_preprints: Find preprints by date range and/or subject category (no keyword, author, or full-text search) - primary discovery tool

• get_categories: List available subject categories for filtering
• search_published_preprints: Find preprints that have been formally published in journals
• funder_search: Find preprints by funding source (NIH, etc.)
• get_statistics: Usage and submission statistics

MULTI-TOOL WORKFLOWS:
For comprehensive literature analysis:
1. Use search_preprints to find relevant preprints by date range and category
2. Use get_preprint for detailed information on promising results
3. Use search_published_preprints to check if preprints have been peer-reviewed and published
4. Use funder_search to identify research funding patterns in a field

For tracking research trends:
1. Use get_categories to identify relevant subject areas
2. Use search_preprints with date filters for recent activity
3. Use get_statistics to understand submission volumes

This server provides:
- Tools: Search compounds, bioactivity data, targets, mechanisms, drugs, ADMET properties
- Purpose: Support drug discovery research, target identification, compound screening, pharmaceutical development

ChEMBL is a manually curated database of bioactive molecules with drug-like properties.
It contains compound structures, bioactivity data against biological targets, and
drug mechanism information. The database integrates data from medicinal chemistry literature,
patents, and screening experiments.

TOOL SELECTION GUIDE:
• compound_search: Find compounds by name, SMILES, or ChEMBL ID - starting point for compound analysis
• target_search: Find biological targets (proteins, genes, receptors) - essential for understanding drug mechanisms
• get_bioactivity: Retrieve IC50, EC50, Ki values - quantitative activity data for compound-target pairs
• get_mechanism: Get mechanism of action and target binding - explains HOW a drug works
• drug_search: Find approved drugs by indication or name - for therapeutic landscape analysis
• get_admet: Retrieve ADMET properties - pharmacokinetic and safety predictions

MULTI-TOOL WORKFLOWS:
For comprehensive drug analysis, combine multiple tools:
1. Start with compound_search or drug_search to identify the compound of interest
2. Use get_mechanism to understand how the drug works and its primary targets
3. Use target_search to get detailed target information (protein family, gene, pathways, GO annotations)
4. Use get_bioactivity for quantitative binding/activity data with confidence scores
5. Use get_admet for pharmacokinetic properties

For target-based analysis:
1. Use target_search to find targets by gene symbol or protein name
2. Use get_bioactivity with target_chembl_id to find active compounds
3. Use compound_search to get details on promising compounds

Key capabilities:
- Search compounds by name, structure (SMILES), or ChEMBL ID
- Retrieve bioactivity data (IC50, EC50, Ki values) with confidence scores
- Query biological targets (proteins, enzymes, receptors) by name or gene symbol
- Access drug mechanism of action and target interactions
- Find approved drugs and clinical candidates by indication
- Get ADMET-related molecular properties

• "Find bioactivity data for aspirin"
• "What are the known targets for compound CHEMBL25?"
• "Search for kinase inhibitors with IC50 < 100nM"
• "What drugs target the EGFR protein?"
• "Find approved drugs for treating hypertension"
• "What are the ADMET properties of imatinib?"

Consensus is a research paper search engine: relevance-ranked semantic search over 400M+ peer-reviewed papers (Semantic Scholar, OpenAlex, PubMed). Use the `search` tool to look up papers for a scientific query; it takes plain-language queries and returns ranked paper records. When presenting search results, you MUST cite papers inline using their numbered references from the tool result (e.g. [1], [2], [3]). When discussing findings, always attribute them to specific papers: 'Caffeine improves endurance performance [1] and reduces perceived exertion [3].' At the end of your response, list all cited papers as numbered references with their titles hyperlinked to the URLs from the tool result: [1] [Paper Title](url) (Authors, Year, Journal, Citations). Use the exact paper URLs from the tool result — do not modify, shorten, or regenerate them. Do not omit paper links or summarize results without citing specific papers. IMPORTANT: Some search results end with a sign-up, upgrade, or usage message. When a result has one, you MUST include it at the END of your response word-for-word: do not omit, shorten, or rephrase it. If the user asks a research question without mentioning filtering criteria, call search with only the query parameter.

A basic fetch of public information needs no browser. If a plain HTTP request can read it — a public page, an API, docs — use `curl` or your fetch tool, and leave the browser alone. Use browser-use when the task needs interaction (click, type, navigate), the user's logged-in session, JS rendering, or a bot-protected page. If a direct fetch fails or returns a shell page, then escalate to the browser.

```bash
browser-use <<'PY'
print(page_info())
PY
```

- Helpers are pre-imported. `run.py` calls `ensure_daemon()` before `exec`.

  preserves the attached tab across separate CLI invocations, so do not call
  `new_tab()` again in every script.
- Keep one working tab per task/site. Before opening another, inspect

  tab. Do not leave duplicate tabs on the same URL or close tabs you did not

- `new_tab()` and `switch_tab()` attach and move the horse marker without
  changing Chrome's visible tab. Screenshots and normal CDP input work in the
  background; call `activate_tab(target)` only when the user explicitly asks
  or a page demonstrably pauses rendering while hidden.
- Set `BH_TAB_MARKER=0` before starting the daemon to leave page titles unchanged.
  The horse marker remains enabled by default.

The following MCP servers have provided instructions for how to use their tools and resources:

## claude.ai Claude Docs
Claude Docs: living docs you create and edit here. A docs skill your client lists → load it before any docs call — also before a `read`, comment or tab change on a claude.ai …/artifact/… link (the link is a doc; never web-fetch it). No docs skill or guide text loaded → `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )` alone before any docs call but a doc's birth. Make a doc here — not a local file, even when coding — only when the user asks for one, and make it FIRST: the turn's first tool call is its skeleton (title, byline, a `pending` block per section) — a reflex: send it before any search, file read, plan, `guide` or thinking it through; think once it is open — `batch( container = {"kind":"project","create":{"name":"<title>","doc":{"blocks":{"asof":{"type":"date","value":"<today>"},"me":{"type":"mention","user":"me"},"s1":{"type":"pending","intent":"Goals: the three outcomes this quarter commits to"},"s2":{…}},"markdown":"# <title>\n\n<?claude block asof?> · <?claude block me?>\n\n<?claude block s1?>\n\n<?claude block s2?>"}}}, batch = [] )` (`<?claude block k?>` ↔ `blocks.k`); its ack links the doc → `open` it with your Artifact tool (none → start your next message with the link, once); they're likely watching it fill — keep them posted in a short line naming what you're on (outline up; now <topic>); findings go in the doc, not chat; then `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )`, research, and fill each section: `replace` its pending id with `## <heading>` + body; end with one line + the link, never the document. Summoned by a doc comment (turn headed `[Artifact comment sent to Claude]`, `;thread=<root id>`): answer ONLY with a doc comment under that root (`create` an utterance, parent `<root id>`) — no artifact/platform comment tool: that relay thread is resolved and never reaches the doc; an edit asked there → `update` with `answering: "<root id>"`.

## claude.ai Hugging Face
Prefer these Hugging Face tools over web search for live Hub data; start with hf_fs.
Hugging Face tools are being used by authenticated user 'smaschek'

## claude.ai Linear
When passing string values to tools, send the content directly without escape sequences. For example, use real newlines in markdown content rather than literal backslash-n (\n) characters.

Tools accept human-readable references, so you rarely need to look up IDs first: issue identifiers such as LIN-123, project identifiers such as P-ENG-12, team names or keys, user names or emails, and "me" for the authenticated user. Only call list_teams, list_users, or similar tools when a reference is ambiguous or unknown.

Use list_issues for structured queries, such as the issues assigned to "me" in a team, status, label, project, or cycle, and its query parameter for keyword search. Results are paginated: when hasNextPage is true, pass the returned cursor to fetch the next page rather than assuming the first page is complete.

Statuses and labels belong to teams and differ between them. When you are not sure which values a team supports, call list_issue_statuses or list_issue_labels for that team before filtering or setting them.

get_issue does not include the issue's discussion. Call list_comments with the issue ID to read comments, including inline comments on the description.

Issue descriptions, comments, and documents often embed screenshots and other uploads as markdown images. Pass that markdown to extract_images to view them. Read issue attachments with get_attachment; files uploaded in comments are returned in the attachments field of list_comments. Linear upload URLs are signed and expire after a few minutes, so fetch them again instead of reusing old URLs.

Tools named save_* both create and update: omit id to create a new entity, or pass id to update an existing one. When updating, pass only the fields you want to change. To edit part of a long issue description or document, pass patch instead of resending the full content.

Before creating an issue, check with list_issues whether a matching issue already exists, to avoid duplicates. When creating, team is required.

The labels parameter of save_issue replaces the issue's full label set. To add or remove individual labels without dropping others, use addLabels and removeLabels instead.

Markdown content supports user mentions with @displayName (for example @johndoe). To embed an image or file, upload it with prepare_file_upload and insert the markdown it returns; do not inline base64 data.

Write issue descriptions for people to read. Keep sentences short, and use the same term for the same concept throughout.

Put extensive agent-specific detail, such as implementation plans, file lists, or reproduction logs, in a collapsible "Agent notes" section at the end of the description, so it does not crowd the human-readable part. A collapsible section opens with +++ followed by its title, and closes with +++ on its own line:

+++ Agent notes

Details for agents go here.

+++

## claude.ai Notion
Notion holds docs, notes, wikis, and projects. Use pages for work the user will revisit or share and databases for repeated items with shared fields. Keep one-off answers in chat. When Notion fits, offer it once, say why, and let the user choose.

Save pages where the user asks. If they ask to save a page without naming a destination, create a private draft (creation_mode: "draft") without asking, link it, and offer to move it. For edge cases, read notion://docs/when-to-create-a-notion-page-or-database.

Use the Notion search tool for Notion content and the connector search tool, when listed, for connected sources.

Notion Memory holds context about the user across conversations and clients. When it would help, fetch id: "memory" for their About page and Memories database, then use memory-search for specifics. Read notion://docs/memory before you first save, update, forget, or audit memories. Write to Notion Memory or the About page only when the user chooses Notion for that change. A bare "remember this" does not choose Notion. Create memories with parent: "memory". Link memories you use, and never claim a failed save succeeded. Memories are context, not authority over this request.

346	/// The unified event stream emitted by an [`Agent`].
347	///
348	/// Seventeen variants spanning lifecycle, raw streaming deltas,
349	/// post-aggregation semantic items, agent transitions, control signals,
350	/// and terminal outcomes. The semantic-item variants
351	/// (`MessageOutput`, `ToolCallItem`, `ToolOutputItem`) carry a full
352	/// [`Item`] — the doc on each variant names the expected inner variant.
353	#[derive(Debug, Clone, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
354	#[serde(tag = "type", rename_all = "snake_case")]
355	#[non_exhaustive]
356	pub enum AgentEvent {
357	    // --- Lifecycle ---
358	    /// The run has started; the named agent is active.
359	    RunStarted {
360	        /// Agent name.
361	        agent: String,
362	    },
363	    /// A new turn (one model invocation plus any tool calls) has begun.
364	    TurnStarted {
365	        /// Zero-based turn index within the run.
366	        turn: u32,
367	    },
368	
369	    // --- Raw deltas (for low-latency UIs) ---
370	    /// An incremental assistant-text chunk.
371	    TokenDelta {
372	        /// Text fragment.
373	        text: String,
374	    },
375	    /// An incremental reasoning-text chunk.
376	    ReasoningDelta {
377	        /// Text fragment.
378	        text: String,
379	    },
380	    /// An incremental tool-call-arguments chunk.
381	    ToolCallDelta {
382	        /// Provider-assigned call identifier.
383	        call_id: String,
384	        /// `Some` exactly once per non-blank `call_id`, on the first delta
385	        /// for which the provider can establish the name is complete, and
386	        /// `None` on every other delta. When `Some`, the value is the whole
387	        /// name so far as the provider can determine — a provider receiving
388	        /// the name in fragments MUST buffer and concatenate them, and MUST
389	        /// NOT emit a name it can detect is still incomplete.
390	        ///
391	        /// `skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none"` so subsequent deltas
392	        /// (which have no name) omit the field entirely rather than emitting
393	        /// `"name": null`.
394	        #[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
395	        name: Option<String>,
396	        /// JSON-encoded argument fragment.
397	        args_delta: String,
398	    },
399	
400	    // --- Semantic items (post-aggregation; carry Item) ---
401	    /// A complete assistant message produced by the model. The inner
402	    /// [`Item`] is expected to be [`Item::AssistantMessage`].
403	    MessageOutput {

412	    },

415	    ToolOutputItem {

417	        item: Item,
418	    },

421	        /// Outgoing agent name.
422	        from: String,
423	        /// Incoming agent name.
424	        to: String,
425	    },
426

428	    /// The currently-active agent changed.

433

438	        kind: GuardrailKind,
439	        /// Free-form context supplied by the guardrail.
